calls.output: Use the Greek yoghurt you have in the pantry in place of the sour cream, but stir it in off the heat and keep the heat very low. Greek yoghurt splits even more easily than sour cream, so let the pan cool for a minute first. Warm it through gently for just a minute or two, without letting it bubble.

Swap the sour cream for the Greek yoghurt, which you have in the pantry. Use the same 200g, but let the pan cool for a minute off the heat first and keep the heat very low, as yoghurt splits even more easily than sour cream. Stir it in gently and warm through without letting it bubble.

Swap the sour cream for the Greek yoghurt, which you have in the pantry. Use the same 200g, but let the pan cool for a minute off the heat first, and stir it in gently over the lowest heat. Yoghurt splits even more easily than sour cream, so don't let it bubble.

Stir in about 100ml of the oat cream, which you have in the pantry, after blending, then warm it through gently on the hob for a minute without letting it boil. Oat cream is dairy-free and gives a smooth, silky finish. Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed.

Stir in about 100ml of the oat cream, which you have in the pantry, after blending, with the soup still hot but off the heat. It adds silky richness without dairy, and you can taste and add a little more, then season with salt. Keep the stick blender in the saucepan for a few seconds more to bring it together.

Stir in about 100ml of the oat cream, which you have in the pantry, after blending, while the soup is still hot. Oat cream is dairy-free, so it makes the soup silky without changing the tomato flavour much. Taste and add a pinch of salt, which you have in the pantry, if needed.

Mix in 2 tablespoons of the ground flaxseed, which you have in the pantry, with 3 tablespoons of water and leave it for 5 minutes to turn gloopy, then stir it through the mash. Add a spoonful of the porridge oats, also from your pantry, if the mix still feels wet. Chill the shaped patties for 10 minutes before frying so they hold together.

Mix in 2 tablespoons of the chickpea flour, which you have in the pantry, as it binds well without egg. Drain and pat the beans dry first, then mash them well so they turn sticky. Chill the shaped patties for 10 minutes so they hold together in the pan.

Use the chickpea flour, which you have in the pantry. Stir in about 2 tablespoons (roughly 20g) and mash the mixture a little more so it turns thick and tacky. Then chill the shaped patties for 10 minutes before frying, so they hold together in the pan.

Use your largest frying pan in steps 2 and 3, adding a little of the vegetable oil, which you have in the pantry. Because it's smaller than a wok, cook the chicken in two batches of about 3 minutes each on high heat so it browns rather than steams. Then stir-fry the broccoli and red pepper for 3-4 minutes, and add the soy sauce at the end.

Use a large frying pan instead of the wok for steps 2 and 3, keeping the heat high and adding a splash of the vegetable oil, which you have in the pantry. Cook the chicken in two batches for about 5 minutes each, since a crowded pan steams it. Then stir-fry the broccoli and pepper for 3 minutes, adding the soy sauce at the end.

Use your largest frying pan in place of the wok for steps 2 and 3. Because it's smaller, cook the chicken in two batches over high heat with the vegetable oil you have in the pantry, allowing about 3 minutes extra in step 2 so it browns rather than steams. Then cook the broccoli and red pepper in the same pan for the same 3 minutes before adding the soy sauce.

Use a small splash of the white wine vinegar, which you have in the pantry. Stir in about 1 teaspoon (5ml) with an extra ladle of the hot chicken stock, which you also have, so the rice still gets a little acidity. Stir until it is absorbed.

Use a small splash of the white wine vinegar, which you have in the pantry. Stir in about 1 teaspoon (5ml) with an extra ladle of the hot chicken stock, which you also have, and stir until it is absorbed. Vinegar is sharper than wine, so keep to that small amount.

Use a small splash of the white wine vinegar, which you have in the pantry, about 1 teaspoon, mixed into an extra ladle of the hot chicken stock, which you also have. Pour it in the same way and stir until it is absorbed. Keep it to that amount, as vinegar is much sharper than wine.

Stir 1 tablespoon of cornflour (which you have in the pantry) into 3 tablespoons of cold water until smooth. Pour it into the simmering stew while stirring, then let it bubble for 2 minutes. Cornflour is gluten-free, and if the sauce is still thin, repeat with a smaller amount.

Mix 1 tablespoon of potato starch (or cornflour, which you have in the pantry) with 2 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, then stir it into the simmering stew. Keep it bubbling gently for 2 to 3 minutes, and it will thicken. If it is still thin, add another half tablespoon of the mixture the same way.

Stir 1 tablespoon of cornflour (which you have in the pantry) into 3 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, then stir it into the simmering stew. Let it bubble gently for 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens. Cornflour is gluten-free, so it is safe for you. If it is still thin, repeat with a little more slurry.

Sprinkle on sunflower seeds, which you have in the pantry. For extra flavour, toast about 30g in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until lightly golden, then let them cool. Scatter them over the noodles just before serving so they stay crunchy.

Sprinkle about 20g of sunflower seeds over the top, which you have in the pantry. For a deeper flavour, toast them in a dry saucepan over a medium heat for 2 minutes, then let them cool. Scatter them on just before serving so they stay crisp.

Sprinkle on about 20g of the sunflower seeds, which you have in the pantry. For more flavour, toast them in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2 minutes, until lightly golden, then let them cool. Scatter them over the noodles just before serving so they stay crisp.

Look at the side of the fillet: the flesh turns opaque and pale pink, and the cooked colour creeps up from the skin about two-thirds of the way. After turning, the salmon is ready when the thickest part flakes easily when you press it gently with the fish slice and is just a little translucent in the very centre. The skin should be crisp and release easily from the pan.

The salmon is done when the flesh has turned opaque and pale pink about three-quarters of the way up the side from the skin, and the fillet flakes easily when you press the thickest part with the fish slice. After turning, the centre should look just slightly translucent, as it will finish cooking from the heat in the pan. The skin should also release easily from the pan, which tells you it is crisp and ready to turn.

The salmon is done when the flesh has turned from translucent to opaque pink about three-quarters of the way up the side, and the fillet flakes easily when you press the thickest part with the fish slice. Turn it only once the skin releases easily from the pan, then give the other side 2 to 3 minutes. The centre should look just barely opaque, still slightly moist.

Stir in about 15ml of coconut aminos, which you have in the pantry, around the edge of the wok so it sizzles and reduces slightly. Toss for 30 seconds to coat the chicken and broccoli, then taste. It adds a deep, savoury-sweet flavour, so you may need only a small pinch of salt, if any.

Stir in about 10ml of fish sauce, which you have in the pantry, and toss it through for 30 seconds so it coats the chicken and broccoli. It adds deep savoury flavour, so taste before adding any extra salt. If it still needs more, add another 5ml.

Stir in about 15ml of coconut aminos, which you have in the pantry, and toss for 30 seconds so it coats the chicken and broccoli. It adds a savoury, slightly sweet depth without any soy. Taste it, and add a pinch of salt only if it still needs it.

Make a quick stock with the white miso paste and dried porcini, which you have in the pantry. Stir about 1 tablespoon of miso into 1 litre of hot water, add a handful of crumbled porcini and a splash of soy sauce, also from your pantry. Keep it hot in the saucepan so it doesn't stop the rice cooking, and taste before adding any salt, as miso and soy are already salty.

Make a quick stock with the white miso paste and dried porcini, which you have in the pantry. Stir about 1 tsp of miso into each 250ml of hot water, then soak a few porcini in it for flavour. Keep it hot in the saucepan and carry on adding it a ladle at a time. Taste before adding any salt, as the miso is already salty.

Make a quick stock with the white miso paste and dried porcini, which you have in the pantry. Stir about 1 tsp of miso into each 250ml of hot water, then soak a few porcini in it if you can spare them. Keep it hot in the saucepan and carry on adding it a ladle at a time. Taste before adding any salt, as miso is already salty.

Jah, suurus on oluline: sammudes 3 ja 4 peavad kartulid ja kanakoivad mahtuma ühe kihina, muidu kartulid aurustuvad ega pruunistu. Jaga need kahele väiksemale ahjuplaadile ja küpseta plaate ahju kahel eri riiulil samal 200 °C juures, vahetades plaatide kohad poole aja pealt. Küpsetusaeg jääb 45 minutiks ning kana sisetemperatuur peab ikka jõudma 75 °C-ni.

Jah, suurus on oluline sammudes 3 ja 4: 1250 g kartulit ja 5 kanakoiba ei mahu väikesele plaadile ühe kihina ning kartulid hakkavad hauduma, mitte pruunistuma. Jaga need väikese plaadi ja ahjuvormi vahel, pane need ahju eri riiulitele ning vaheta kohad küpsetusaja keskel. Aeg ja 200 °C jäävad samaks.

Jah, suurus on oluline, sest sammudes 3 ja 4 peavad kartulid ja kanakoivad mahtuma ühe kihina, muidu kartulid aurustuvad ega pruunistu. Jaga kõik kahele väikesele ahjuplaadile ja küpseta need korraga ahju eri riiulitel, samuti 200 °C juures. Vaheta plaatide kohad umbes 22 minuti pärast, et kõik pruunistuks ühtlaselt.

Kasuta hapukoore asemel Kreeka jogurtit, mis sul söögikapis olemas on. Lisa sama kogus, 160 g, aga võta pann enne tulelt maha ja sega jogurt kastmesse alles siis, kui see on veidi jahtunud. Hauta siis tasasel tulel edasi ja ära lase keema tõusta, muidu jogurt lõheneb.
